new_entities.name: APOE ε4-tailored diet strategy
new_entities.description: Dietary recommendations or lifestyle nutrition strategies tailored specifically to APOE ε4 carrier status.

new_entities.name: Cognitive outcomes
new_entities.description: Changes in memory, executive function, global cognition, or related cognitive-performance measures.

edges.effect_quant: In the FINGER subgroup analysis, cognitive benefits from a multidomain lifestyle intervention were seen in both APOE ε4 carriers and noncarriers, with no strong evidence that genotype-specific diet tailoring itself was the decisive ingredient. The 2025 PENSA trial in APOE ε4 carriers with subjective cognitive decline also did not show a statistically significant primary cognitive advantage at 12 months for the intensive lifestyle-plus-EGCG strategy over the comparison arm.
edges.population: older adults or at-risk adults whose dietary or lifestyle advice is tailored according to APOE ε4 genotype
edges.mechanism: APOE ε4 may modify lipid handling, glucose vulnerability, or dementia risk trajectories, but translating that biology into a proven genotype-specific dietary prescription remains difficult.
edges.summary: This is a mixed precision-nutrition edge rather than a validated genotype-based prescription. APOE ε4 status is relevant to risk stratification, but the evidence does not yet show that APOE-specific diet tailoring reliably improves cognition beyond broader healthy lifestyle approaches.
edges.caveats: Many studies bundle diet with exercise, cognitive training, or supplements, so the diet-specific contribution is hard to isolate. Risk prediction should not be confused with evidence for a successful personalized nutrition treatment.

evidence.citation: Solomon A et al 2018 JAMA Neurol
evidence.notes: Effect of the Apolipoprotein E Genotype on Cognitive Change During a Multidomain Lifestyle Intervention: A Subgroup Analysis of a Randomized Clinical Trial.

evidence.notes: A multimodal lifestyle intervention complemented with epigallocatechin gallate to prevent cognitive decline in APOE- ɛ4 carriers with Subjective Cognitive Decline: a randomized, double-blinded clinical trial (PENSA study).
